data.name: Ghassana
data.gender_notes: Ghassana is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'ghasasan', meaning 'to give good news'. This name symbolizes the joy and hope that comes with the arrival of a newborn. The name Ghassana carries the meaning “Giver of Good News” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ghassana usually hope their child will grow to embody giver of good news and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghassana total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

It reflects the best of emotions experienced by parents upon the arrival of a newborn child. The tradition of naming infants after positive attributes in the Islamic faith is well established, and Ghassana exemplifies this perfectly. It is a name that radiates with love, joy, and excitement.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ghassana also carries a deeper spiritual significance in the Islamic faith. It reminds us of the joyful news delivered by the angels Gabriel (Jibreel) and Michael (Mikail) to the Prophet Muhammad when he was given the message of the divine revelation. The name is a constant reminder to be grateful for the blessings bestowed upon us, particularly the gift of life and the arrival of a newborn. It is also a reminder to spread good news and positivity to others, bringing joy and happiness to those around us.
